publisher: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), Working Group I
series: IPCC emission scenarios: IS92 (1992 Supplementary Report, Section A3 'Emissions Scenarios for the IPCC: an Update')
notes: Six scenarios IS92a-f. Only IS92a has a table of global emissions (Tables A3.7, A3.11, A3.12: 1990, 2000, 2025, 2050, 2100). IS92b-f values are printed only in figures, so they are captured as the published ranges. IS92a values for 2010 and 2020 and CO2 concentrations are IPCC restatements from TAR WG I Appendix II (2001), flagged with published_in.

entries.subject: global greenhouse gas emissions pathway
entries.quote: IS92a includes only those policies affecting greenhouse gas emissions which are agreed internationally or enacted into national laws (as of December 1991). [Table A3.1: World Bank 1991, 11.3 B by 2100; economic growth 1990-2025: 2.9%, 1990-2100: 2.3%; 12,000 EJ Conventional Oil, 13,000 EJ Natural Gas]
entries.note: Bracketed part is from Table A3.1 (read from the page image).

entries.subject: global greenhouse gas emissions pathway
entries.quote: IS92b, a modification of IS92a, suggests that current commitments by many OECD Member countries to stabilize or reduce CO2 might have a small impact on greenhouse gas emissions over the next few decades, but would not offset the substantial growth in the rest of the world.

entries.subject: global greenhouse gas emissions pathway
entries.quote: IS92c has a CO2 emission path which eventually falls below its 1990 starting level. It assumes that population grows, then declines by the middle of the next century, that economic growth is low, and that there are severe constraints on fossil fuel supplies.

entries.subject: global greenhouse gas emissions pathway
entries.quote: IS92d | UN Medium-Low Case, 6.4 B by 2100 | 1990-2025 2.7%, 1990-2100 2.0% | Oil and gas same as "c"; Solar costs fall to $0.065/kWh; 272 EJ of biofuels available at $50/barrel | Emission controls extended worldwide for CO, NOx, NMVOC and SOx. Halt deforestation. Capture and use of emissions from coal mining and gas production and use.
entries.note: Table row, cells joined with '|'; read from the page image (the OCR text of this rotated table is unusable).

entries.subject: global greenhouse gas emissions pathway
entries.quote: The highest greenhouse gas levels result from IS92e which combines, among other assumptions, moderate population growth, high economic growth, high fossil fuel availability and eventual hypothetical phase-out of nuclear power.

entries.subject: global greenhouse gas emissions pathway
entries.quote: IS92f | UN Medium-High Case, 17.6 B by 2100 | 1990-2025: 2.9%, 1990-2100: 2.3% | Oil and gas same as "e"; Solar costs fall to $0.083/kWh; Nuclear costs increase to $0.09/kWh | Other: Same as "a" | CFCs: Same as "a"
entries.note: Table row, cells joined with '|'; read from the page image.

entries.subject: global CO2 emissions from fossil fuels and industry
entries.metric: CO2 emissions from fossil fuels, range of IS92a and IS92b
entries.quote: IS92a and b, which most resemble the SA90 in terms of assumptions for key parameters, show a range of emissions of 10.3 to 10.7 GtC in 2025, and 18.6 to 19.8 GtC in 2100.
entries.note: Range over two scenarios. The per-scenario IS92b value is not printed as text or table.

entries.subject: global CO2 emissions from fossil fuels and industry
entries.metric: CO2 emissions from fossil fuels, range of the six IS92 scenarios
entries.quote: The range of emissions estimated for the wider set of alternative scenarios is 7 to 14 GtC in 2025 and 5 to 35 GtC in 2100.
entries.note: Range over all six scenarios. Per-scenario values for IS92b-f appear only in figures (Section A3); not read.
